skills.principle: When an authoritative correction supersedes an input used by a prior conclusion, invalidate that conclusion and recompute every dependent result from the corrected input while preserving unchanged rules and assumptions.
procedure: Identify the original input, its authoritative replacement, and the prior conclusion that depended on it.
Treat the replacement as current and the superseded input as unusable.
Trace which parts of the prior conclusion were derived from the superseded input.
Retain only relationships, rates, offsets, durations, and other assumptions that remain valid and were not corrected.
Recalculate the affected outputs using the corrected input and the retained derivation rules.
Check that no stale value from the invalidated conclusion remains in the result.
preconditions: A later statement explicitly or authoritatively replaces an earlier input.
The earlier conclusion depends on the replaced input.
The derivation rule connecting the input to the requested output is known or can be reliably inferred.
Any assumptions retained during recalculation have not themselves been superseded.
counter_indications: Do not apply this procedure when the new information is merely an alternative, hypothetical, or unverified claim rather than a superseding correction.
Do not revise a conclusion that is independent of the corrected input.
Do not reuse the old derivation rule if the correction also changes that rule, policy, dependency, or calculation method.
Do not invent missing relationships or assumptions when the available information is insufficient to recompute the result.

skills.principle: When a corrected source value supersedes an earlier value, invalidate every dependent conclusion and recompute it from the corrected value while preserving unchanged quantities, rules, and relative offsets.
procedure: Identify the authoritative corrected value and treat the superseded value as unusable.
Determine which parts of the prior conclusion depended on the superseded value.
Recover the calculation, timing relationship, or other transformation that produced the prior conclusion.
Substitute the corrected value while retaining only assumptions and relationships that were not changed.
Recompute all affected outputs and check arithmetic, units, ordering, and internal consistency.
Answer with the updated result and, when useful, briefly indicate that it replaces the prior conclusion.
preconditions: A correction clearly supersedes an earlier source value.
The requested conclusion directly or transitively depends on that superseded value.
The original dependency rule or relationship can be inferred or is explicitly provided.
No instruction states that the remaining assumptions or relationships have also changed.
counter_indications: Do not apply the procedure when the requested result is independent of the corrected value.
Do not preserve prior offsets or formulas when the correction explicitly replaces the entire plan, rule, or method.
Do not invent missing dependency rules when the available information is insufficient to recompute the result.
Do not use the superseded value merely because it appeared earlier or was stored in prior state.

skills.principle: When an input is superseded, invalidate conclusions that depend on it and recompute them using the corrected input while preserving the original relationship or calculation.
procedure: Identify the old input, its corrected replacement, and the prior conclusion marked as invalid.
Trace how the prior conclusion was derived from the old input, including any quantities, offsets, durations, dependencies, or formulas.
Replace only the superseded input with the corrected value unless other information is also explicitly revised.
Reapply the original derivation rule to calculate the updated conclusion.
Answer with the recomputed result and, when useful, briefly indicate that it reflects the correction.
preconditions: A previous conclusion depends on an input that has been explicitly corrected or superseded.
The dependency rule or calculation connecting the input to the conclusion is available or can be reliably inferred.
The remaining inputs and assumptions have not been invalidated.
counter_indications: Do not apply this procedure when the correction is unrelated to the requested conclusion.
Do not recompute when the corrected input or required dependency rule is missing or ambiguous; request clarification instead.
Do not preserve the original derivation rule if the correction also changes the formula, duration, scope, sequencing, or other assumptions.
Do not use the superseded conclusion or old input as current truth.

skills.principle: When a corrected source fact invalidates a conclusion derived from it, discard the old conclusion and recompute it from the corrected fact while preserving the original dependency rules and offsets.
procedure: Identify the source fact that was explicitly superseded and treat only its corrected replacement as current.
Mark every conclusion that depended on the superseded fact as invalid rather than repeating or lightly editing it.
Recover the transformation used in the original reasoning, including ordering, duration, lead time, lag time, and other constraints.
Apply that same transformation to the corrected source fact.
Check that the recomputed result is internally consistent and directly answers the requested field.
Report the new result clearly, optionally noting that it replaces the prior invalid conclusion.
preconditions: A source fact has been explicitly corrected or superseded.
The requested conclusion depended on that source fact.
The relationship between the source fact and conclusion can be inferred from the prior reasoning or stated constraints.
No other relevant dependency or rule has been superseded.
counter_indications: Do not apply this procedure when the correction is unrelated to the requested conclusion.
Do not preserve the original transformation if the correction also changes the governing rule, duration, offset, sequence, or scope.
Do not calculate a precise replacement when the dependency is ambiguous or required information is missing; request clarification instead.
Do not use the invalidated conclusion as authoritative after its supporting fact has been superseded.
